assumptions.text: 1 stream-aligned team, core-team, owns all 6 contexts: the operator and the fleet of AI agents (manifest scale_target notes; understand N6; strategize N3). The size is not recorded because the number of agents changes from run to run and has no cap (understand C13).

1 deployable unit, the horch binary, holds all 6 contexts as modules inside horch-core. The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34; understand C1, N6; decompose N1). Decision D1 records the options.

The fleet-run wrapper and horch fleetd check are process roles of the same horch binary, not deployables. The design maps the wrapper to today's horch worker subcommand (design: Where multi-herdr stands today) and names horch fleetd check as a horch command (design: Architecture and roles). The owning context of the wrapper is still open (connect D2, Q1); the deployable is the same for every answer.

The data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose.

The questions table belongs to ideas, as decompose D2 recommends (still open): the sub-orchestrator answers worker questions and ideas emits own-assumption-recorded and question-answered (connect F5). If decompose D2 or the operator inbox owner (decompose Q3) goes to task-execution, the questions table moves with it.

herdr, the agent CLIs, git, GitHub and the OS service managers are external systems behind adapters in fleet-runtime and the other owning contexts. None is a deployable of this design (strategize N1; design: Architecture and roles).

The cognitive load of core-team is high: 6 contexts and 2 core contexts (task-execution, integration). No second team exists to take a context, so the mitigation is module boundaries that a test enforces, 1 context per task where possible, and the 8 migration phases that add the contexts one at a time (understand C9).

Each context owns its workspace folders inside the 1 deployable: ideas owns the idea folders (ai_docs/plans/<run>/, design /fleet/ideas/), task-execution owns the task and attempt folders under the state root, worker-profiles owns the teammate profile files (understand N17; design: Workspace layout and file protocol).

open_questions.text: Where does docs sync run: as a horch subcommand that fleetd schedules inside the 1 deployable, or as the separate agent-docs-sync binary that grows from crates/herdr-docs-sync (decision D2)? No context owns docs sync yet (decompose Q2).

Must a test enforce the module boundaries of the 6 contexts (for example an arch_scan rule: no context writes the tables or folders of another context)? This is the main mitigation of the high cognitive load (A7).

notes_for_downstream.text: The 1 deployable runs in 4 process roles of the same horch binary: the fleetd daemon (horch fleetd, the only ledger writer, runs the reconcile pass of all 6 contexts), short-lived CLI commands (read the ledger read-only, send requests on the command channel), the fleet-run wrapper (1 per attempt), and horch fleetd check (the heartbeat check). The module of a context can run in more than 1 role; only the fleetd role writes the ledger.

Sharpens decompose N5: each context owns its own ledger tables and workspace folders (A4, A8). fleet-runtime commits the write, but only the owning context decides the rows of its tables. No context reads or joins the tables of another context; it uses that module's contract or its events.

teams.name: Operator and agent fleet
teams.notes: 1 human operator plus a changing number of AI agents (no cap, understand C13). Runs the horch binary on the operator's machine; reached through the horch CLI, herdr panes and the needs-you folder. Load is high because the team owns 6 contexts and 2 core contexts. Mitigation: no second team exists, so keep each context a module with its own tables and folders, enforce the boundaries with a test (Q2), give an agent 1 context per task where possible, and add the contexts in the 8 migration phases.

deployables.name: horch binary
deployables.rationale: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI, the daemon and the wrapper always have the same version and horch self-update restarts the daemon on the new binary (design: Amendments D9, FM-34; understand C1). All 13 relationships are in-process calls and events (connect N1), task-execution reaches worker-profiles and fleet-runtime with synchronous calls (connect F2, F4), and 1 team owns every context. No split reason is in the inputs. Released through horch self-update and the GitHub release assets (understand C7).

scale_check.note: 1 of a 1-1 target. Why not fewer: 1 is the minimum. Why not more: ideas, integration and worktree-custody have async-only inbound, but no input gives a split reason (no independent scaling, runtime, regulation, stack or second team), the design requires 1 binary so the CLI and daemon cannot differ in version (D9, FM-34), the only ledger writer is 1 process (understand C4), and task-execution, worker-profiles and fleet-runtime are joined by synchronous calls (connect F2, F4).

decisions.question: Is the fleetd design 1 deployable, or do the daemon or the fleet-run wrapper ship as their own binaries?

options.summary: 1 modular monolith: the horch binary holds all 6 contexts; fleetd, the CLI commands, the wrapper and fleetd check are process roles of it.
pros: The CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (FM-34)
horch self-update replaces 1 release asset and restarts the daemon at once (D9)
Matches connect: all 13 relationships are in-process
cons: 1 team carries 6 contexts in 1 codebase; the load is high (A7)
A fault in any module can stop the 1 daemon process
risks: Modules reach into each other's tables and the context boundaries erode without a test (Q2)

options.summary: 2 deployables: a fleetd daemon binary and the horch CLI binary, joined by the command channel.
pros: The daemon can restart or update without a new CLI
cons: The CLI and the daemon can have different versions, the failure FM-34 prevents
2 release assets for horch self-update (understand C7)
risks: Old code acts on a newer ledger, or the reverse (FM-34)

options.summary: 2 deployables: the horch binary and a separate small fleet-run wrapper binary launched once per attempt.
pros: The wrapper process is small and starts fast
The wrapper can be built without the ledger code
cons: A second release asset and a second version to keep in step
Today the wrapper is the horch worker subcommand; a split adds work for no stated need
risks: A wrapper of an older version writes heartbeat.json or exit.json in a shape fleetd no longer reads

decisions.rationale: The design settles it: fleetd is a subcommand of the single horch binary, so the CLI and the daemon cannot have different versions (design: Amendments D9, Migration plan, FM-34). The manifest target is 1 to 1.
would_flip_if: The operator changes D9 and accepts a daemon that updates apart from the CLI
fleetd must run on a different machine from the CLI
A second team takes a context and needs its own release train

decisions.question: Where does docs sync and adapter conformance run: inside the 1 deployable or as its own job binary?

options.summary: A horch subcommand inside the 1 deployable that fleetd schedules daily and on a CLI version change. Recommended.
pros: Keeps the 1-1 scale target and 1 release asset
fleetd sees a CLI version change first and can start the run at once (FM-19)
A drift becomes a task through the only ledger writer
cons: Moves crates/herdr-docs-sync code into the horch binary
The horch binary gets the docs fetch and mirror code
risks: A slow docs fetch runs inside the daemon and delays the reconcile pass, unless it runs as its own process role

options.summary: A separate agent-docs-sync job binary, widened from crates/herdr-docs-sync as design Docs sync says, run on a schedule.
pros: Follows the design text: generalise crates/herdr-docs-sync into agent-docs-sync
The daemon never runs network fetches for docs
cons: A second deployable breaks the 1-1 scale target
A second release asset and a second scheduler entry on 3 OSes
risks: The job and the daemon disagree on the profile health format after an update

options.summary: A development tool in the repository only; the conformance results ship inside each horch release.
pros: No runtime code on the user's machine for docs sync
cons: A CLI update between 2 horch releases is not caught before dispatch, which FM-19 requires
Contradicts design: Docs sync runs daily and on any CLI version change
risks: Every worker of an updated CLI fails until the next horch release (FM-19)

decisions.rationale: Recommendation A: it keeps the fixed target of 1 deployable and lets fleetd react to a CLI version change. The strongest argument against A: the design says to generalise crates/herdr-docs-sync, which is its own binary today, and B follows that text. The design does not say whether the widened tool ships in the horch binary, so the operator decides.
would_flip_if: The operator wants docs sync to run when fleetd is down
The docs fetch needs network access that the daemon must not have

plain_words.what: We decided who owns each part of fleetd and how many separate programs ship.
plain_words.decided: 1 team (the operator and the AI agents) owns all 6 parts. All 6 parts ship in 1 program, the horch binary, as separate modules.
plain_words.assumed: Each part keeps its own database tables and folders inside that 1 program, and no part edits another part's tables.
plain_words.riskiest: 1 team owns 6 parts, 2 of them core. If nothing checks the module walls, the parts tangle and a later split costs much more. Where docs sync runs is still open (D2).
